findings.short_summary: Filter-view re-assertion not implemented in code
findings.summary: SHEET-TAB-003 spec text explicitly mandates 'republish actively re-asserts saved Sheets Filter Views so they persist across the rewrite'; all three A outputs (A1, A2, A3) implement this via fetch-before-clear + re-apply-after-write pattern; code (adapters.rs:214-237, testkit.rs:158-192) contains zero filter-view logic.
findings.failure_scenario: Spec requires: User sets a filter on Positions tab → republish rewrites data → filter definition should survive. A outputs implement: read filter metadata, clear data, write new data, restore filters. Code does: clear data, write data, done—filters lost on overwrite.
findings.description: The real EARS spec (provided) explicitly requires filter-view preservation across republish. All three A-side implementations (A1, A2, A3) unanimously and correctly interpret this requirement and implement filter fetching+restoration. Every B-side reconstruction (B1, B2, B3) correctly observes the code has no filter-view logic. This is a clear spec→code gap: spec-stated behavior is not implemented.

findings.short_summary: Tail truncation enforced; residual rows deleted on republish with fewer rows
findings.summary: Code enforces: wholesale row replacement (testkit.rs:178 `existing.rows = tab.rows.clone()`), leaving exactly N rows when republish carries N rows; any prior stale rows beyond the new set are deleted (tail-truncated). Spec text makes no mention of residual-row cleanup or exact-row-count guarantee. B outputs all explicitly reconstruct this behavior (B1, B2, B3 all mention 'tail-truncate', 'exact row count', 'residual rows deleted'). A outputs are less explicit (most focus on wholesale replace, some vague on tail cleanup).
findings.failure_scenario: Prior republish: 10 data rows. New republish: 5 rows. Spec silent. Code guarantees: exactly 5 rows afterward (rows 6–10 deleted). A outputs don't explicitly require this; B outputs identify it as code-enforced invariant.
findings.description: The code enforces an exact-row-count guarantee—if you republish with N rows, the tab has exactly N rows after, with no leftover stale tail. The spec text does not state this boundary condition. This is a code-side enforcement that goes beyond spec text (undocumented behavior surfaced by B-side reconstructions).

findings.short_summary: Cell typing (Value vs Formula) parsing rule undocumented in spec
findings.summary: Code enforces: Cell::Value cells written via adapters.rs:217 as plain text (Sheets parses per user-input rules: bare '15' as numeric, '15.0000%' as numeric fraction 0.15); Cell::Formula cells written with '=' prefix (live formulas). This is critical for post-tax estimate columns (Est. Unrealized Tax = Unrealized P&L × Est. Tax Rate) where Est. Tax Rate (a Value cell formatted '15.0000%') must coerce to 0.15 for multiplication. Spec text silent on this Value/Formula split and parsing convention. B outputs all reconstruct: 'cell typing per column is stable', 'value cells parse per user input', 'formula cells live'. A outputs assume the distinction exists but don't detail Sheets parsing semantics.
findings.failure_scenario: Est. Tax Rate rendered as string '15.0000%' (not parsed). Formula =G*H tries to multiply string × number → fails or yields wrong result. Code guarantees: Value cells written as userEnteredValue (Sheets parses) so '15.0000%' becomes 0.15; formulas read it as numeric 0.15 and multiply correctly.
findings.description: Code enforces a Sheets-API-specific parsing rule (userEnteredValue for Values, formula strings with = for Formulas) that is fundamental to correct formula recalculation but never mentioned in the spec text. This is a code-side refinement not in spec—behavior the B outputs correctly identify.

findings.short_summary: Write-lock serialization before workbook mutation undocumented
findings.summary: Code enforces: advisory write-lock acquired before any workbook mutation (lib.rs:964-972); if lock unavailable, republish returns `published: false` (non-destructive refusal); lock released after tab writes. Spec text makes no mention of concurrency control, lock-based serialization, or partial-refusal semantics. B outputs all surface: 'acquired advisory write-lock before mutation', 'not-published refusal if lock unavailable', 'serialization via lock'. A outputs make no mention of locking.
findings.failure_scenario: Two sync cycles try to republish concurrently. Spec silent on conflict. Code: first acquires lock, publishes; second sees lock unavailable, returns not-published, waits for next cycle (no concurrent writes). A outputs don't address; B outputs observe this as enforced concurrency boundary.
findings.description: Code models a concurrency-control pattern (lock-before-mutate + deferred-retry-on-unavailable) that is not mentioned in the spec text. This is a code-side enforcement of a behavioral boundary the spec doesn't make explicit.

findings.short_summary: Frozen header enforced with loud panic (code tightens spec intent)
findings.summary: Spec implies (by exclusion: data 'overwritten by design') that header should survive republish. Code enforces this with an unconditional assertion panic (testkit.rs:174-176: 'frozen header must never be rewritten'). A outputs mostly mention 'never rewritten' but don't specify enforcement (silent acceptance or panic?). B outputs all identify the assertion as enforcement mechanism ('panic, not silently accepted'). Spec text does not say how to handle header mismatch; code says: panic loudly.
findings.failure_scenario: Republish presents a different header (e.g., column renamed). Spec silent on error handling. Code: assertion failure (panic). A outputs: mostly silent on enforcement. B outputs: correctly identify loud panic as enforcement.
findings.description: Both A and B surface frozen-header survival (spec intent implied, A and B agree). Code goes beyond spec by enforcing it with a loud panic. This is a case where code tightens spec intent with explicit failure rather than silent acceptance—agreement across directions on the core behavior, but B correctly identifies the implementation detail (panic) the spec doesn't state.

notes: Classification: BD-DRIFT (both directions surface gaps in different domains—A: missing feature spec requires; B: multiple behaviors code enforces but spec doesn't mention). Stability within each direction: HIGH (A outputs unanimously implement filter preservation; B outputs unanimously identify code lacks filters and correctly observe cell typing, truncation, locking). Finding rankings ordered by impact: (1) Filter-view re-assertion gap (CRITICAL, explicit spec requirement unmet), (2) Tail truncation (HIGH, code enforces undocumented boundary), (3) Cell typing parsing (HIGH, critical for formula correctness, undocumented), (4) Frozen-header assertion (MODERATE, code tightens spec with loud enforcement), (5) Write-lock serialization (MODERATE, concurrency model undocumented).
